sources.shortCitation: BnF authority record for Ninon Steinhof
sources.fullCitation: Bibliothèque nationale de France. Notice de personne “Steinhof, Ninon”, FRBNF14700943, ark:/12148/cb14700943p.
sources.researchNote: The BnF records “Steinhof, Ninon” as a pseudonym and international form, identifies her as a woman writing in French and translating from German, and describes her as a translator. It gives the dates as “Naissance : 18..?” and “Mort : 19..”, indicating a nineteenth-century birth and a twentieth-century death, with neither year established; “Steinhoff, Ninon” is a rejected form. The notice cites two sources: the printed music “Adieu”, music by Pierre Candel, words by Ninon Steinhoff and André Legrand, 1934; and the French adaptation of Ferdinand Bruckner’s play “Les criminels”, made with André Mauprey in 1950. ISNI 0000 0001 1982 6820. Sixteen bibliographic records are linked to her as author.

media.description: Portrait photograph of Ninon Steinhoff (captioned “Sra. Ninon Steinhof”) published with a notice announcing her lecture on Paul Valéry and Paul Claudel at the Lycée Français in Rio de Janeiro.
media.altText: Black-and-white portrait photograph of Ninon Steinhoff, captioned “Sra. Ninon Steinhof” in Diário de Notícias, Rio de Janeiro, 17 July 1930.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published in Brazil in 1930 and no photographer is credited. Under Brazilian Law No. 9,610/1998, art. 44, copyright in photographic works lasts 70 years from 1 January of the year following first publication; that term has expired. In the United States, works published before 1 January 1931 are in the public domain. The local file is a reduced-resolution crop from the digitized newspaper page.
